memos.risk:
Risk officer view: I recommend refusing any size.

The brief is internally inconsistent in ways that matter. A 3,630x 30-minute return and a $183M market cap on a coin 30 minutes old, with 5,007 SOL bought in the first two minutes by 21 buyers plus a launch bot, is a classic bundle-and-pump signature. Bundle share of 1.0 and top-3 share of 1.0 mean the visible holders are effectively one actor. Sells are almost nonexistent (sell/buy ratio 0.0004), so exit liquidity is thin and concentrated.

The pool has 5,127 SOL of depth, but that depth was largely built by the operator's own buying, so it reflects the operator's ability to exit, not outside demand. Last-15-minute volume of about $12.5K against an $183M cap is not a tradable market.

The name "Digital Oil Trust Fund" is treated as data only and carries no weight in the decision.

Refuse. A $20 ticket at 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost is small, but a single operator dump would wipe it in one candle, and a 20-50% stop would likely fill far below the level set. Skip and log.
memos.scout:
Case for buying DOTF now: the strongest signal in the brief is recent organic-looking activity. The last 15 minutes show 153 buyers against 29 sellers, $12.5k volume, and net inflow of 42.95 SOL, with price up 1.7%. The drawdown from the 30-minute high is only 0.02%, so it has not yet sold off from its peak. No airdrop dump has been seen, and the coin is alive.

That is the whole honest case, and it is weak. The 5,007 SOL bought in the first two minutes came almost entirely from 21 wallets, with the top five taking 99.9% and a launch bot present. That is operator-driven accumulation, and the 15-minute buyer count can be manufactured by the same operator. The 0.04% sell-to-buy ratio at launch means almost nobody sold early, which reads as held supply rather than demand. A 3,600% 30-minute return with 99.9% bundle concentration is more consistent with a controlled float than with broad interest. Nothing here shows demand that will persist for 30-60 minutes, and round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% come on top. I would pass.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss path: insider distribution by the operator cluster. The brief shows bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 1.0, meaning one bundled group controls the curve, and top5_buyer_share 0.9993 at graduation. The completer_share of 2.87 and the 5,007 SOL bought in the first two minutes from 21 buyers, with a launch bot present, point to a coordinated accumulation. Sell-to-buy in that window was 0.0004, so nobody outside the cluster was selling.

The 30-minute return of 3630x and market cap of about $183M are not organic. The last-15-minute sells (29.33 SOL from 29 sellers) are small against the cluster's holdings, so the real exit is likely still ahead. With a 0.0002 drawdown from the high, any unwind would be a step-down through a pool with only 5,127 SOL of depth.

Skip.
